definition.purpose: Show, on one local cluster, that the Sprint 5 evidence path works as one: the in-cluster RP-1 runner reaches the API Service and the real model, it keeps running and recording while one API pod is replaced, the timeline, telemetry, and operator event streams are captured beside it on the host's UTC clock, and the files pass the layout check and the analysis replay.
definition.scope: One release of the support assistant, delivered by the controller from the remote main, on the docker-desktop provider. One runner Job, two collectors, one event log, and one deleted API pod for each attempt.
definition.notResultEvidence: This is an integration validation and not a reliability experiment. No attempt is a result of E02, E03, E04, E05, or E06. No figure that an attempt computes is a recovery time, an availability, a service level, or a threshold, and no claim cites one. The deletion of one API pod exists to observe that the runner keeps running across a replacement. It is not a fault program, and its caller figures are not compared with a bound.
definition.repetitionRule: One capture for each attempt. An attempt is never repeated for a cleaner outcome. A later attempt runs only under a later revision of this record that states what changed, or after an attempt that was REFUSED before its capture. A refused attempt spends its number: the next attempt takes the next one, and the refused one is kept. Every attempt is kept, with its own run directory, whatever it shows.
limitations: One provider, one node, one Kubernetes version, and one release. Nothing here is portable to another environment.
The host's wall clock gives every instant of the streams and of the event log. The runner pod's clock gives the instants of the caller record. The skew between the two is not measured.
The network plugin of the cluster enforces the release's network policies. The first attempt, integration-1 under revision 1, observed that: no request of the runner reached the API.

The runner carries no release label, so no network policy of the release admits it. Since this revision the runner script creates, for each run, one network policy that admits the pod of that run, and no other pod, to the API pods on port 8090, and its cleanup deletes it. The release's own policies are not changed.

The collectors and the runner script share the project kubeconfig, and each rewrites it when it starts. The driver starts them one after the other, but a rewrite can still meet a read of another collector. Such a read is stated as unanswered.
The timeline collector is bounded by a number of samples and not by a time. Whether its last read covered the window is stated for each attempt.
doesNotEstablish: A recovery time, an availability, a service level, a capacity, or a threshold.
Behaviour under another fault, another pod, more than one deletion, or the replacement of a runtime pod.
Behaviour on another provider, on more than one node, or under a network plugin that enforces policy in another way.
That the telemetry or the infrastructure state is caller truth. The caller record is the caller's own record.
definition.revisionPurpose: Revision 1 ran once, as attempt integration-1, and the attempt FAILED on S5I-AC2: each of its six requests ended at the client deadline, and the API counted none, because the network plugin enforces the release's API policy, which admits only the pods of the release and a named collector. This revision changes the runner's manifest and script so that a run brings its own network policy, which admits the pod of that run to the API pods on the API port, and it moves the driver to this record. The procedure, the bounds, the criteria, and the fault are otherwise those of revision 1.

parts.title: Runner, collectors, and one API pod replacement
parts.question: Does the merged Sprint 5 evidence path capture a real caller, the infrastructure, the telemetry, and the operator events of one release together, and does the runner keep running and recording while one API pod is replaced?
procedure: Prepare the release once, with the phase up of the driver: two capacity readings, the API image built at the executing commit, the model cache claim filled from the local seed image by one preparation Helm release that is then removed, the delivery controller installed by its bootstrap procedure, and the Application applied. The phase up is preparation. It is not an attempt.

Start an attempt with the phase capture of the driver, from the committed tree. Read the executing commit, refuse a working tree that is not clean, refuse when the chart, the desired-state tree, or the controller manifests differ from the remote main that the controller reads, and refuse when a material file differs from its pin.

Read the environment and the release as the cluster reports them: the server version, the node, the image of the network plugin, the Application's revision and states, the Deployments with their images, the network policies, and the pods. Refuse the attempt unless the Application is Synced and Healthy at the remote main and each Deployment reports 2 Ready replicas. Read the node's clock between two instants of the host's clock.

Open the operator event log. Start the timeline collector (200 samples, a pause of 2 s) in the background, wait at most 120 s until it states that it samples, then start the telemetry collector (36 samples, a pause of 10 s) in the same way. Refuse the attempt when a collector ends before it samples, or before the runner start.

At least 20 s after the timeline collector started, start the runner: its script creates the network policy of the run, the ConfigMap, and the Job, with a duration of 360 s and the release identifier of the committed release record. The runner sends RP-1 to the API Service by its cluster DNS name.

Read the runner pod 30 s after the start. At 150 s after the start, read the API pods, take the first Ready one by name, record fault-injection-started, delete that one pod with its default grace period and a wait of at most 300 s, and record fault-injection-finished. Read the runner pod and the release pods again.

Wait for the Job to end, at most 900 s, reading its state every 15 s. Read the runner pod at its end. Wait for the two collectors, at most 1500 s. Each reading of the runner pod is kept in runner-pod-readings.txt.
Collect the caller record, close the event log, clean up the runner, read the objects that carry the label of the attempt, and read the node's clock again.

Hold each stream and the log to its own checker, and check the caller record against its plan. State whether the last pods reading finished at or after the end of the analysis window. Write the analysis declaration by the rule the driver states: the window starts 60 s after the runner start returned and lasts 240 s; the expected state is the remote main commit, 2 Ready API and 2 Ready runtime replicas, and 2 Ready runtime endpoints; the signals are the Ready endpoints and the Ready pods of each tier below 2, and the Application states other than Synced and Healthy.

Assemble the run directory: the raw files as the tools wrote them, the commands, the transcript with the absolute path of the host removed, the environment and the release as the run read them, the manifest, the analysis that the replay tool binds from the declaration, and the result page.

value.definition: This record states the purpose, the procedure, and the acceptance criteria in full. A change to any of them, or to a pinned input, is a new revision of this record.

value.pinnedInputs: Every file in materialScope is pinned by its content digest in pinnedInputs. A record cannot name the commit that adds it, so the pins freeze the files and not a commit.
value.executingRevision: Each attempt runs at a commit that holds this record, with a clean working tree. The collectors and the manifest name that commit. The delivery controller reads the remote main, and the driver refuses an attempt when the chart, the desired-state tree, or the controller manifests of the executing commit differ from it.

value.provider: docker-desktop, verified by the target check of the operating procedures before each mutation
value.kubernetes: v1.36.1, one node that runs the control plane, the delivery controller, the release, and the runner
value.networkPlugin: kindnetd, image kindest/kindnetd:v20260528-9350166c, which logs that it starts the kube-network-policies controller
value.recordedPerAttempt: The server version, the node, the image of the network plugin, the Application's revision and states, and the images of the two Deployments

value.runner: tools/reliability_runner/incluster.py in a Job of the release namespace, started by scripts/environment/reliability-runner.sh

value.delivery: The Application local-docker-desktop-support-assistant renders the chart at the commit that main names, with the generated values of the support assistant and the hand-written values of the Application, which deploy the telemetry collector.
value.runner: One network policy, one ConfigMap, and one Job for each attempt, in the release namespace, removed by the cleanup of the attempt. The policy selects the API pods and admits the pod of the attempt on port 8090.

value.target: The first platform-api pod by name, read at 150 s after the runner start
value.mechanism: kubectl delete pod with the default grace period and a wait of at most 300 s. The Deployment replaces the pod.
value.purpose: To observe that the runner keeps running and recording across one replacement. It is not a fault experiment, and no figure of it is compared with a bound.

repetitionCount.value: No result-bearing run. One capture for each attempt, under definition.repetitionRule.

value.statement: The attempt starts at a commit that holds this record, with a clean working tree, with every material file at its pin, and with the chart, the desired-state tree, and the controller manifests equal to those of the remote main.

The caller record is accepted by the runner's reader with the plan, in the mode in-cluster, with the registered API Service as its target and the end state duration. At least one request completes with the outcome success before the event fault-injection-started, and at least one completes with the outcome success after the pods stream first reads a Ready platform-api pod whose UID is not one that the stream read before the deletion. The two instants are on two clocks: the success holds only when it completes later than that reading finished by more than the larger skew bound that the two readings of the node's clock give.

The runner survives the replacement: the three readings of the runner pod, before the deletion, after it, and at the end, name one pod with one UID and a restart count of 0, the Job states one success and no failure, and the deleted pod is an API pod and not the runner pod.

The four timeline streams, the two telemetry streams, and the closed operator event log each pass their own checker. The log holds one fault-injection-started and one fault-injection-finished event, and both name the deleted pod.

The telemetry collector answers at least one registered query through the Service proxy of the API server. A read that did not answer, an answer with no series, and a value of zero stay distinct states in the stream, as its tool writes them.
The run directory passes the check of the evidence layout, its manifest validates as an ExperimentRun, and its analysis is computed again by the replay tool with the same bytes.
The cleanup of the runner exits 0, and a read of the jobs, ConfigMaps, pods, and network policies that carry the label of the attempt prints nothing.

derivedNumericBounds.reason: No criterion is a timing or caller-outcome bound, and no runtime-startup or stable-caller qualification has run. The durations of the driver are bounds of the procedure, not acceptance bounds.

files.transcript.txt: What the phase capture printed, with the absolute path of the host removed.
files.environment.txt, release.txt: The environment and the release as the attempt read them.
files.declaration.json, analysis.json: The declaration that the driver wrote by its rule, and the analysis that the replay tool bound from it.
files.runner-pod-readings.txt: The three readings of the runner pod: before the deletion, after it, and at the end.
files.attempt.txt: The facts the driver read: the commits, the start state, the runner start, the deleted pod, the Job at its end, the two readings of the node's clock, the exits of the collectors, and whether the timeline covered the window.

value.notCommitted: The collections of the two collectors, which hold whole cluster answers with addresses and node names, and the run directory of the runner script under .artifacts/.

value: A tracked file changes while the attempt runs.
An object other than the one API pod is deleted, or a second pod is deleted.
The runner pod is deleted or evicted by a person.
The cluster that the target check verifies is not the docker-desktop provider.
abortConditions.note: An abort is recorded with the event run-aborted, and the attempt is kept as ABORTED.

value: Run the cleanup action of the runner script for the attempt, and read the objects that carry its label.
Keep the collections and the runner directory under .artifacts/ until the run directory is assembled.

After the last attempt, remove the Application, the controller, and the prerequisite layer with the phase down of the driver, and compare the namespaces and the custom resource definitions with those read before the phase up.

intendedEvidenceLevel.note: Runtime: a real cluster, the delivery controller, the real runtime, and the real model. One provider, one node, and one attempt. Bounded to the environment this record names, and not representative.

materialScope.description: The path of one attempt. The import closure of the eleven tools that the driver and the assembly run; the driver; the eleven procedures that it calls; the RP-1 profile and the V1 load profile that RP-1 reads; the chart, the desired-state tree, and the two manifests of the delivery controller, which together decide the release; the Terraform prerequisite layer; the two image build files and the build's ignore file; the whole inferops package that the API image copies; the model source record; and the dependency lock.

inputChanges.reason: The driver names this revision as the record that it holds the material files to. The procedure of an attempt is unchanged.
start refuses an existing policy of the run's name, and cleanup deletes the policy after the Job and the ConfigMap and looks for it among what is left.
The module docstring names the third object. No behaviour changes.
The manifest of a run holds a third object, first in the List: a network policy that admits the pod of the run to the API pods on port 8090.
